title: Reliability Playtest Charter: Feature-embedded SLO Adoption (Q3 2025)
content:
Purpose
---
Run a small, timeboxed playtest to validate a lightweight pattern for embedding SLO ownership in feature teams (not just platform teams). Goal is to surface operational work early, test tooling gaps, and iterate on a pragmatic SLO onboarding checklist we can scale. This is intentionally scoped: playtest = learning, not rollout.

Summary / TL;DR
- 6-week playtest (Aug 4 - Sep 12 2025) across 3 feature services (search-rewrite, realtime-embeds, session-router).
- Deliverables: per-service SLO proposal, minimal instrumentation, error-budget burn simulation, two runbook updates, a short retro with quantified recommendations.
- Success if runbooks allow an oncall to restore to green for 80% of simulated incidents within target RTO and teams report the pattern is actionable.

Why this playtest?
- Many teams can declare SLOs but lack a repeatable onboarding flow and lightweight instrumentation templates.
- We want to check whether feature teams can own SLOs without central SRE doing the bulk of work for each service.
- Hypothesis: with a 1-page checklist + a telemetry template + a 1-hr SLO triage drill, teams can reach minimum viable SLO ownership.

Scope (what's in / out)
- In: three services across product verticals chosen for operational diversity; basic SLI definitions (latency & success rate); deploy a small amount of signal-mirroring; simulated error-budget burn exercises; short-runbook edits and oncall drill.
- Out: company-wide rollout, deep kernel/runtime changes, provider-level (cloud infra) contract changes, formal SLA creation.

Testbed services (owner + quick note)
- search-rewrite (owner: Marcus Lee) — CPU-bound, heavy prefix caching; p50/p95 latency critical for UX
- realtime-embeds (owner: Claire Huang) — GPU-backed async inference callers; higher variance; interesting KV cache behavior
- session-router (owner: Diego Alvarez) — auth+routing layer, low-latency fanout, important for multi-region failover

Experiment hypotheses
1) A one-page SLO checklist reduces onboarding time by 60% vs current ad-hoc approach.
2) Instrumentation templates (prometheus metrics + tracing span names) let SRE-less teams detect and escalate incidents earlier (median detection time improvement).
3) Error-budget drills reveal at least two common tooling gaps (alert fatigue & incomplete traces) that we can fix with <2 sprint effort.

Concrete success metrics (measurable)
- Per-service: defined SLO doc (yes/no) and proposed thresholds within week 1.
- Observability: p95 request latency and success rate SLIs instrumented and flowing to dashboards by end of week 2.
- Runbook effectiveness: during simulated incidents, 80% of oncall responders can restore service to standard health within target RTO for that service.
- Adoption signal: each feature lead rates the process >= 4/5 usefulness at retro.

Playtest timeline (high level)
- Week 0 (prep, Jul 28 - Aug 3): finalize service selection, instrument templates, coordinate calendar for drills.
- Week 1 (Aug 4 - Aug 10): kickoff + define SLOs & SLIs; owners fill template.
- Week 2 (Aug 11 - Aug 17): implement metrics; small dashboards; baseline runchecks.
- Week 3 (Aug 18 - Aug 24): runbook draft + small tabletop exercise.
- Week 4 (Aug 25 - Aug 31): simulated error-budget burns (controlled chaos) + live oncall drill 1.
- Week 5 (Sep 1 - Sep 7): iterate on alerts, trace coverage; live oncall drill 2 (post-fixes).
- Week 6 (Sep 8 - Sep 12): retro + deliverables handoff + recommendations doc.

Roles & responsibilities
- Playtest lead: Priya Menon — overall run, synthesize results, coordinate cross-team scheduling.
- SRE liaison: Asha Patel — instrumentation guidance, alert tuning, runbook review.
- Feature leads: Marcus, Claire, Diego — implement templates, attend drills, own runbook edits.
- Observability engineer: Tom Baker — dashboard templates and metric pipelines.
- Product PM observer: (optional) — watch for UX impact and escalate requirements.

Minimal instrumentation checklist (must-haves)
- Request-level success/failure counter (tagged by route/handler)
- Request latency histogram (p50/p90/p95) with backend vs client timing if available
- In-flight tokens / queue length for services with batching
- Trace root span with consistent name and critical child spans (model call, cache hit/miss)
- Synthetic probe (synthetic traffic) for end-to-end from ingress -> egress (low frequency)

Alerting & escalation pattern (lightweight)
- Tier 1: page @oncall if error-rate exceeds threshold for X minutes OR p95 latency > threshold for Y minutes.
- Tier 2: notification to feature lead + SRE liaison if error budget burn > Z%/hour.
- Use burn-rate based incident classification (experimental): fast-burn escalates faster, slow-burn scheduled check-in.

Playtest runbooks (deliverable)
- 1-page runbook template (what to check, quick remediation steps, key dashboards links).
- Triage checklist for first 15 minutes (collect traces, check synthetic, rollback toggle).
- Post-incident: short blameless incident note template and follow-up actions.

Simulation plan (controlled)
- Failures injected by feature teams in coordination: latency injection, increased error codes, partial region isolation for session-router.
- Each simulation has a small blast radius, documented rollback, and SRE liaison present.
- One scenario will simulate degraded model backend for realtime-embeds to test KV cache fallback and model variant routing.

Data to collect during playtest
- Time to detect (TTD), time to acknowledge (TTA), time to restore (TTR) per incident drill.
- Error budget burn curves for each simulated exercise.
- Number of missing spans/trace gaps observed per drill.
- Owner feedback survey (5 questions) and freeform notes.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: drills cause customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: keep synthetic traffic and small blast radius; deploy to staging-like environment where feasible; emergency rollback plan.
- Risk: alert noise overwhelms oncall. Mitigation: pre-flight alert tuning; Mute non-actionable alerts during drills; SRE liaison to adjust in real time.
- Risk: insufficient participation. Mitigation: calendar invites in advance, timeboxed work, leadership ask-in for feature leads.

Communication plan
- Weekly sync (30m) with feature leads + SRE liaison (Mon).
- Slack channel: #playtest-reliability (create with pinned templates and schedule).
- Post-playtest doc + 1-pager summary to reliability guild and product leadership.

Questions / open decisions (notes-to-self)
- Do we run drills in prod or staging for session-router? prefer staging but need to validate multi-region failover which looks prod-only.
- What error-budget burn thresholds are realistic for the feature teams? default Z=10%/hour for fast-burn test?
- Need a lightweight permission for the SRE liaison to mute alerts during drills. Who owns that?

Deliverables (end of playtest)
- Completed per-service SLO proposals and agreed thresholds (doc).
- 1-page runbook template + two filled runbooks.
- Instrumentation checklist + dashboards per service.
- Playtest report: metrics, key gaps, prioritized fixes (backlog sized).
- Recommendation: scaleable SLO onboarding flow + proposed owner for rollout (tentative: eng-sre + product-platform).

Next steps (immediate)
- Confirm service owners by Jul 22.
- Finalize simulation scenarios and rollback plans by Jul 28.
- Create Slack channel and calendar series by Jul 30.
- Ship SLO + metric templates to feature leads by Aug 1.

Notes for retrospective focus
- Which fixes were <2 sprint work and unblock adoption?
- Which require cross-org policy or tooling changes?
- Can the 1-page checklist be adapted into a GitHub template for PRs?

Appendix: quick templates (in-doc)
- SLO proposal header: service, owner, SLI definitions, SLO target, measurement window, error budget policy, alert thresholds.
- Runbook 1-pager sections: symptoms, quick checks, mitigation steps, postmortem link, playbook owner.

-- End of charter --

(Comments: keeping this intentionally lean — aim for tight experiments and actionable outputs. We'll iterate the artifacts into a Confluence playbook after the run.)
